svg.title: A count that can be held, and says what it will do
svg.desc: Finding 7 · by reading · the two times that answer for the user, and one that takes words away A discussion mockup drawn by hand from the built-in theme's colours, not a screenshot.
svg.text: A count that can be held, and says what it will do
Finding 7 · by reading · the two times that answer for the user, and one that takes words away
NOW
Fixed, and not held by being there
DIRECTION
Set, held, and started again by a hand
1 Restart, asked: left alone for a minute
Restart now?
Restarting in 60 seconds
Whatever is not saved in open
programs will be lost.
Restart
Cancel
At nought it restarts. Enter restarts. The minute is fixed (ADR 88)
Nothing holds it: not a key, not the pointer on the box
Raised by a press that slipped, it ends the session by itself
2 The screens stood another way: fifteen seconds to say so
Keep the screens like this?
Enter keeps them. Escape, or 12 seconds,
puts them back.
Fifteen seconds to find the box, read it and reach Enter
No buttons: a pointer cannot answer it at all
Fixed, and right to be short: a screen may have gone dark
3 A notification, with the pointer resting on it
Anna
Are you there?
Gone at five seconds all the same, and kept nowhere to read again
A sender's own time beats notifications.timeout: 0 (“until clicked”)
Volume and brightness: a second and a half, whatever is set
Four more, fixed today
Two presses as one: 400 ms, within 4 units
The lock screen left alone: 30 s, and the field is emptied
A fullscreen window's bar: rest 600 ms, gone after 1 s
A tooltip: 500 ms (known)
1 Restart, asked: left alone for a minute
Restart now?
Restarting in 60 seconds
Whatever is not saved in open
programs will be lost.
Restart
Cancel
The keyboard is on Cancel, as on the lock screen's own question
Any key, or the pointer moving, starts the count again
power.wait: 60 in config.yaml; 0 waits for an answer
2 The screens stood another way: fifteen seconds to say so
Keep the screens like this?
They go back in 12 seconds
Keep
Put back
Buttons, so that a pointer can answer; the keyboard on Put back
A key or the pointer starts the count again, so it cannot run out
under a hand that is at work; left alone, it still goes back
3 A notification, with the pointer resting on it
Anna
Are you there?
Held while the pointer or the keyboard is on it, and shown to be
“Until clicked” means it, whatever the sender asked for
The level stays as long as other notices do, when that is longer
And those four
mouse.double_click, as every desktop has it
What was typed kept while the screen rests, or the rest a setting
A key that brings the bar back, as well as the edge
A tooltip that shows with the keyboard on its thing
